column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines AI-native software development, focusing on how developers collaborate with AI coding agents within structured software engineering workflows. Intended for third- and fourth-year B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering students, the course addresses the core challenges of defining developer intent, managing context resources, and coordinating agentic tools. Students learn to configure agent workspaces using the Model Context Protocol, design executable software specifications from ambiguous requirements, instrument human-agent development loops to diagnose context failure modes, and establish continuous verification pipelines using synthetic defect injection. Additionally, students evaluate software quality metrics to refactor agent-generated technical debt across multi-turn workflows. The course is not a general introduction to artificial intelligence or basic programming, but a specialized study of collaborative human-AI software engineering. Instruction is delivered through a combination of lectures, tutorial sessions, and hands-on laboratory work, culminating in practical project development.

Course Code: Configure AI coding agent environments and context resources, given a multi-component software specification and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool definitions, such that all required tool invocations and context retrievals complete without protocol errors.
column2: Construct executable software specifications and test-driven prompt context from ambiguous functional software requirements, using structured spec-driven development methods, such that at least 80% of generated code modules satisfy all specified unit tests on first synthesis.
column3: Diagnose failure modes and context drift in human-agent iterative development loops, given execution traces and interaction logs from an automated AI software factory workflow, identifying at least three distinct root causes of sub-optimal code generation with supporting log evidence.
column4: Analyse automated testing and verification pipelines for agent-generated software components, using synthetic defect insertion and automated regression suites in a continuous integration environment, determining code coverage gaps and identifying at least 90% of introduced functional defects.
column5: Evaluate the reliability and maintainability of AI-assisted software projects across multi-turn human-agent collaborative workflows using standardized software quality benchmarks, justifying each architectural refactoring recommendation against quantitative reliability and maintainability metrics.
